$comment: Desired Cloudflare Tunnel ingress for the demo box, plus the DNS shape each
public hostname must have. This file is the single source of truth for which
hive hostnames are public and what they reach.
The tunnel is remotely managed: cloudflared on the box runs `tunnel run` with
only a TUNNEL_TOKEN, so it pulls its ingress from Cloudflare rather than from
a local config file. That is why this mapping used to exist nowhere in the
repository, and why a stale hostname could point at a decommissioned VM for
weeks without any review catching it.
tunnel_id is not a secret: it is already published as the public CNAME target
of every hostname below. The tunnel TOKEN is the secret and is never stored
here.
The `config` object below is the exact body accepted by
PUT /accounts/{account_id}/cfd_tunnel/{tunnel_id}/configurations.
Run `npm run cloudflare:check` to diff this file against live Cloudflare.
Every hostname served by the tunnel must be a proxied CNAME to
<tunnel_id>.cfargotunnel.com. Anything matching managed_suffix that is not
in the ingress list below is drift and the check fails on it. That is
exactly the cp-hive.scubed.co defect: a proxied A record to 40.233.86.19,
a retired VM, which returned 522 on every path while looking like a live
outage of a service that was in fact healthy under a different hostname.

unmanaged.hive.scubed.co: marketing site on Cloudflare Pages (hive-website-9c1.pages.dev), not tunnel-served

ingress.$service: control-plane. Public on purpose: payment-rail webhooks and callbacks must reach it. All /internal/* routes are token-gated and answer 401 from the public internet.
Caddy in front of Open WebUI (Caddyfile.owui)
Caddy in front of the web-console container (Caddyfile.console)
Catch-all. Any hostname without an explicit rule above gets a clean 404 rather than a hanging origin connection.
